questions.question: In a new Angular v21 project, which function in `main.ts` starts the application?
questions.explanation: Standalone apps start with `bootstrapApplication`, passing the root component and an `ApplicationConfig` whose `providers` build the root injector. `bootstrapModule` is the legacy NgModule entry point.
optionNotes: Legacy NgModule bootstrap; still works but not generated by the CLI.
Not the standard entry point for an app with a root component.
`enableProdMode` only toggles dev checks and is not needed with the CLI.

questions.question: Since which Angular version are components standalone by default, so that `standalone: true` no longer needs to be written?
questions.explanation: Standalone components arrived in v14 (stable in v15) but required `standalone: true`. Since v19 it is the default; a component that belongs to an NgModule must now say `standalone: false`.

questions.question: Your app must read the API base URL from `/config.json` before any component renders, so one Docker image can be promoted across environments. What is the modern way?
options: Read it in the root component constructor with `fetch`
Load it in `ngOnInit` of every service that needs it
Use `provideAppInitializer(() => inject(ConfigService).load())` where `load()` returns a Promise
questions.explanation: App initializers run during bootstrap, and Angular waits for a returned Promise or Observable before creating the root component. `provideAppInitializer` (v19+) replaces the `APP_INITIALIZER` multi-provider.
optionNotes: The root component may render children before the fetch completes.
Services have no `ngOnInit` (only `ngOnDestroy`), and this duplicates the loading.
Environment files are baked in at build time, so you need one build per environment.

questions.question: A standalone component uses `<app-order-card>` in its template but the build fails with "is not a known element". What is the most likely fix?
questions.explanation: A standalone component is its own compilation context: everything its template uses must be listed in its own `imports`. Schemas only silence the error and break type checking.
optionNotes: Standalone components cannot be declared in an NgModule.
That hides the error; the component would never be instantiated.
Providers are for DI, not for template dependencies.

questions.question: Which statements about the Angular CLI build in v17+ are true? (Select all that apply)
options: The default application builder bundles with esbuild
The dev server is based on Vite
Templates are compiled in the browser by default (JIT)
Webpack is still the default bundler for new projects
questions.explanation: The application builder (`@angular/build:application`) uses esbuild for bundling and Vite for `ng serve`. AOT compilation is the default, so the template compiler is not shipped to the browser.
optionNotes: AOT is the default for both build and serve.
Webpack is the legacy `browser` builder.

questions.question: A team upgrades a mature zone.js-based app from v20 to v21 with `ng update`. What happens to change detection?
options: The app keeps using zone.js; zoneless is the default only for newly generated projects unless you opt in
The app automatically becomes zoneless because zoneless is the v21 default
The build fails until `provideZonelessChangeDetection()` is added
zone.js is removed but Default components are converted to OnPush
questions.explanation: Zoneless is the default for new projects since v21. Existing apps keep their zone.js setup (Angular keeps zone-based behaviour for them) and migrate deliberately by removing `zone.js` from polyfills and adding zoneless providers after making components OnPush-safe.
optionNotes: Silently switching would break apps that depend on zone.js triggers.
Nothing is required; existing apps continue to work.
Angular never changes your component strategies automatically.

questions.question: What is the main reason AOT compilation is preferred over JIT for production?
options: It is the only mode that supports two-way binding with `[( )]`
Templates compile at build time: no compiler shipped, faster startup, template errors fail the build
It is required for components to be lazy loaded with `loadComponent`
It removes the need for change detection at runtime
questions.explanation: With AOT the template compiler runs during `ng build`, producing JavaScript instructions. The browser downloads less code, does less work at startup, and type errors in templates are caught before deployment.

questions.question: Which file in a v20+ CLI project holds application-wide providers such as `provideRouter` and `provideHttpClient`?
questions.explanation: `app.config.ts` exports the `ApplicationConfig` passed to `bootstrapApplication`. `angular.json` configures the build, and `app.routes.ts` only holds the route array.

questions.question: What does `[(value)]="qty"` expand to?
questions.explanation: Two-way binding ("banana in a box") is property binding to `value` plus event binding to `valueChange`. A `model()` input creates both for you.

questions.question: The list below is refreshed from the API every 30 seconds (new objects, same ids). Which `track` expression avoids recreating every row?
questions.explanation: Angular uses the track key to match old and new items. A stable unique key lets it keep existing DOM rows when the data is re-fetched. Tracking by object identity treats every refreshed object as new.
optionNotes: New object references on every refresh mean every row is destroyed and recreated.
Works only if the list never reorders; inserts shift every key.
`$count` is the same for every item.

questions.question: Inside a child component, what happens with this code?
options: `name` is updated and the parent sees the new value
It throws at runtime only in dev mode
It fails to compile: an `input()` signal is read-only and has no `set` method
questions.explanation: `input()` returns an `InputSignal`, which is read-only inside the component to enforce one-way data flow. Use `model()` for a value the child may change, or emit an `output()`.

questions.question: Which API declares a two-way bindable input in modern Angular?
questions.explanation: `model()` creates a writable signal input plus a matching `<name>Change` output, enabling `[(name)]` in the parent.

questions.question: A `Card` component wraps `<ng-content>` in `@if (expanded())`. The projected content contains a component that makes an HTTP call in its constructor. What happens while `expanded()` is false?
options: The projected component is not created, so no HTTP call is made
Angular throws an error because ng-content cannot be inside @if
The projected component is still created by the parent, so the HTTP call is made even though it is not displayed
The component is created lazily the first time `expanded()` becomes true, then cached
questions.explanation: Projected content is instantiated by the parent as part of its own view, regardless of where (or whether) the child renders `<ng-content>`. For conditional or lazy content, accept an `<ng-template>` and render it with `ngTemplateOutlet`.

questions.question: Which statements about view encapsulation are true? (Select all that apply)
options: `Emulated` is the default and scopes styles by adding generated attributes to elements and selectors
`ShadowDom` uses the browser's native Shadow DOM
Global styles in `styles.scss` cannot affect elements inside an Emulated component
questions.explanation: Emulated rewrites selectors with attributes like `_ngcontent-xyz`. `ShadowDom` uses native shadow roots. `None` makes the component's styles global. Emulated stops styles leaking out, but global styles still apply inside.
optionNotes: `None` makes styles global, it does not keep them scoped.
Global styles do apply; only component styles are scoped.

questions.question: In a template, `{{ total() }}` calls a plain class method that loops over 5,000 order lines. What is the main problem and the modern fix?
options: No problem: Angular caches method results automatically
The method runs on every change detection check of the component; replace it with a `computed()` signal
Methods cannot be called in templates; use a getter
It causes a memory leak; unsubscribe in `ngOnDestroy`
questions.explanation: Template expressions are re-evaluated whenever the component is checked. A plain method re-computes every time. `computed()` memoises and only recomputes when the signals it reads change. A pure pipe is the older alternative.
optionNotes: Angular does not memoise method calls.
Methods are allowed; getters have the same cost.
No subscription is involved.

questions.question: You need a reference to a child `ChartComponent` in your own template to call its `refresh()` method. What do you use?
questions.explanation: `viewChild` queries the component's own template. `contentChild` queries projected content. `inject` would look for a provider, not a child in the view.

questions.question: Which hook order is correct for the first render of a component with bound inputs?
questions.explanation: After the constructor: `ngOnChanges` (inputs set), `ngOnInit`, `ngDoCheck`, `ngAfterContentInit`, `ngAfterContentChecked`, `ngAfterViewInit`, `ngAfterViewChecked`.

questions.question: What happens when this component is created?
options: It logs the bound order id
Reading a required input before it is set throws an error
questions.explanation: Inputs are bound after construction. Reading a required signal input before it has a value throws (NG0950). Use `computed`, `ngOnInit`, or an effect instead.

questions.question: A parent does `this.items.push(newItem)` on an array bound to a child's `@Input() items`. The child computes a total in `ngOnChanges`. Why is the total stale?
options: The child must implement `ngDoCheck` to receive inputs
Arrays cannot be passed as inputs
`ngOnChanges` fires only when the input reference changes, and `push` keeps the same reference
questions.explanation: Input changes are detected by reference (`===`). Mutation keeps the same array, so no change is recorded. Pass a new array (`[...items, x]`) or use signals with `update`.

questions.question: You need to initialise a third-party chart library on a canvas element in an app that also uses SSR. Where should that code go?
questions.explanation: `afterNextRender` runs once after Angular has rendered the app to the DOM, only in the browser, so the canvas exists and SSR never executes the DOM code. The element is not available in the constructor, and `ngOnInit` also runs on the server.

questions.question: What is the modern replacement for the `destroy$` Subject + `takeUntil` pattern for unsubscribing in a component?
options: `ngOnDestroy` is no longer needed because Angular unsubscribes everything automatically
questions.explanation: `takeUntilDestroyed()` completes the stream when the surrounding `DestroyRef` (component, directive or service) is destroyed. Called outside an injection context it needs a `DestroyRef` argument.
optionNotes: Only the `async` pipe and `toSignal` clean up automatically; manual subscriptions do not.
No such Angular API exists.
`first()` changes semantics and still leaks if no value arrives.

questions.question: What is wrong with this code?
options: Without an argument it needs an injection context, so in `ngOnInit` it throws; pass a `DestroyRef`
questions.explanation: Without arguments, `takeUntilDestroyed` calls `inject(DestroyRef)`, which only works in an injection context such as a constructor or field initialiser. In lifecycle hooks, pass `this.destroyRef` obtained with `inject(DestroyRef)` in a field.

questions.question: For a parent component with one child component in its template, which happens first?
options: Both run at the same time
It depends on the change detection strategy
questions.explanation: The parent's view is only initialised once its child views are. Order: parent init and content hooks, then the child's full set including `ngAfterViewInit`, then the parent's `ngAfterViewInit`.

questions.question: Which lifecycle hook is also called on services?
questions.explanation: Services get `ngOnDestroy` when their injector is destroyed (for example a component-level provider when the component goes away). Other hooks are only for components and directives.

questions.question: With `ChangeDetectionStrategy.OnPush`, which of these does NOT mark the component for check?
options: A property of an object input is mutated by the parent
A `(click)` handler in its template fires
A signal read in its template changes
A new object reference passed to one of its inputs
questions.explanation: OnPush compares inputs by reference, so mutating a nested property is invisible. Events from its template, a new input reference, a template-read signal change, the `async` pipe and `markForCheck()` all mark it dirty.

questions.question: In a zoneless app, a Default-strategy component runs this code. What does the user see?
options: An error, because setTimeout is not allowed without zone.js
"Loading" stays on screen until something else triggers change detection
questions.explanation: Without zone.js nothing tells Angular that a plain field changed in a timer callback. Make `status` a signal (`status.set('Loaded')`) or call `markForCheck()`.

questions.question: What is the difference between `markForCheck()` and `detectChanges()`?
options: They are aliases for the same operation and can be used interchangeably
`detectChanges` only works with zone.js, while `markForCheck` only works when zoneless
`markForCheck` checks only child components; `detectChanges` checks the whole application tree
`markForCheck` flags the view and ancestors for the next pass; `detectChanges` checks this subtree right now
questions.explanation: `markForCheck` is a cheap flag that makes OnPush ancestors visit this view in the next pass (and schedules one in zoneless apps). `detectChanges` is a synchronous check of this subtree.

questions.question: Which of the following trigger change detection in a zoneless Angular app? (Select all that apply)
options: Setting a signal that a template reads
A `(click)` listener bound in a template
Resolving any Promise in application code
questions.explanation: Zoneless Angular reacts to explicit notifications: template-read signal changes, template and host listeners, `markForCheck` (used by the `async` pipe), `ComponentRef.setInput` and view attachment. Promise resolution was only a trigger because zone.js patched it.
optionNotes: Only zone.js treated arbitrary async completions as triggers.

questions.question: This child component throws `ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenChecked` in dev mode. What is the best fix?
options: Wrap the `set` call in `setTimeout` so it runs after the current pass
Call `cdr.detectChanges()` right after setting the title to re-render
Set the title where it is owned (the parent or the route `title`) before the parent is checked
Switch the child to OnPush so the parent is not re-checked
questions.explanation: The parent already rendered `layout.title()` in this pass, then the child changed it during the same pass, breaking unidirectional flow. `setTimeout` and `detectChanges` hide it at the cost of a second render. The fix is to set the state where it is owned, before rendering.

questions.question: Why do signals allow more targeted change detection than `markForCheck()`?
options: Angular knows which views read a signal, so it marks only those views for refresh instead of marking every ancestor dirty
Signals run change detection in a Web Worker
Signals bypass the DOM and update the screen directly
Signals disable change detection for the component
questions.explanation: Templates are reactive consumers. When a signal changes, Angular marks the consuming view for refresh and flags ancestors only as having a child to refresh, so clean OnPush parents are traversed without re-evaluating their own bindings.

questions.question: When is `ExpressionChangedAfterItHasBeenChecked` thrown?
options: In production builds when a binding is slow
In dev mode, when a binding changes between a check and the verification pass after it
When an observable errors in a template
When two components share a service
questions.explanation: Dev mode runs an extra check after each pass and compares bindings. A difference means state changed during rendering. Production skips the check, so the inconsistency is hidden, not fixed.

questions.question: In a zone.js app, a `mousemove` listener on `document` added by a charting library makes the app sluggish. What was the classic fix?
options: Switch every component to Default strategy
Register the listener inside `ngZone.runOutsideAngular()` and re-enter only when state must change
questions.explanation: zone.js triggers application-wide change detection after every patched event. Running the listener outside the Angular zone avoids that. In zoneless apps this concern disappears.

questions.question: What does this log?
options: It throws because computed is read-only
questions.explanation: `computed` derives its value from `count` and recomputes lazily on the next read after `count` changes.

questions.question: Which API should you use for a value derived from other signals, such as a cart total?
questions.explanation: `computed` is pure, memoised and read-only. `effect` is for side effects such as logging or localStorage, not for producing state.

questions.question: Why does this not update the view?
options: Signals cannot hold arrays, only primitive values and plain objects
`push` is not allowed on arrays returned from a signal in strict mode
You must call `items.update()` with no arguments to trigger a refresh
The array is mutated in place, so the reference is unchanged and `Object.is` sees no change
questions.explanation: Signals notify only when the new value differs from the old one by their equality function (`Object.is` by default). Mutating returns the same reference. Use `items.update(a => [...a, x])`.

questions.question: A product list input can change, and the selected product should default to the first item but remain user-selectable. Which API fits best?
options: A `signal` plus an `effect` that sets it whenever `products` changes
questions.explanation: `linkedSignal` is writable (the user can select) and resets when its source changes. `computed` is read-only, and an effect that copies state is the anti-pattern `linkedSignal` replaces.
optionNotes: Read-only: the user could not change the selection.
Works, but creates two sources of truth and an extra update round.
`toSignal` converts Observables, not signals.

questions.question: What is the type of `user` here, and why?
options: `User`, because the HTTP call always emits before the first render
`User | undefined`, because there is no value before the first emission
questions.explanation: `toSignal` subscribes immediately but needs a value before the first emission. Without `initialValue` (or `requireSync: true` for synchronous sources) the type includes `undefined`.

questions.question: Inside an effect you need the current user id for logging, but the effect should re-run only when `cart` changes. What do you use?
questions.explanation: `untracked` reads signals without registering dependencies, so only `cart` triggers the effect.

questions.question: Which statements about computed signals are true? (Select all that apply)
options: They are lazy: they recompute only when read after a dependency changed
They are memoised: repeated reads return the cached value
Dependencies are fixed at creation time
Writing to another signal inside `computed` is the recommended way to sync state
questions.explanation: Computeds track dependencies dynamically on each run (only branches that execute are tracked), recompute lazily and cache. Writing signals inside a computed throws.
optionNotes: Tracking is dynamic per run.
Computeds must be pure; writes throw.

questions.question: For a typeahead that debounces input and cancels stale HTTP requests, what is the recommended approach in modern Angular?
options: Only signals with an effect that calls the API on every change
RxJS (`debounceTime`, `switchMap`) for the event stream, exposed to the template with `toSignal`
questions.explanation: Signals model state and have no time or cancellation operators. RxJS handles events over time; `toSignal` turns the result into state for the template.

questions.question: What does `httpResource` return?
options: A resource whose `value`, `status`, `error` and `isLoading` are signals
questions.explanation: `httpResource` makes the HTTP request through `HttpClient` and exposes the result and request state as signals, re-fetching when signals read in its request function change.

questions.question: In this resource, which signals cause a reload when they change?
questions.explanation: `params` is tracked like a computed; `loader` is not tracked. Reading `lang` inside the loader uses its current value but does not trigger reloads. Put it in `params` if it should.

questions.question: What happens if the `params` function of a resource returns `undefined`?
options: The previous value is cleared and an error is set
The resource stays idle and the loader is not called
questions.explanation: Returning `undefined` from `params` means "no request yet", for example while a route id is missing. The resource goes to `idle` and the loader is skipped.

questions.question: Why is `httpResource` usually preferred over a `resource` whose loader calls `fetch` for your own API?
options: `fetch` cannot parse JSON responses without an extra library
It uses `HttpClient`, so interceptors, testing tools and SSR transfer cache apply
`resource` loaders cannot be cancelled when params change
`httpResource` caches every response forever, so it is faster
questions.explanation: A raw `fetch` bypasses `HttpClient`: no auth or error interceptors, no testing utilities, no transfer cache. `resource` is for non-HTTP async sources.

questions.question: The id changes from 1 to 2 while the request for 1 is still in flight. What does `httpResource` do?
options: Waits for request 1, then sends request 2
Sends request 2 and shows whichever response arrives last
Ignores the change until `reload()` is called
questions.explanation: Like `switchMap`, a resource aborts the previous load when params change. `resource` passes an `abortSignal` for this; `httpResource` and `rxResource` cancel automatically.

questions.question: Which statements about resources are true? (Select all that apply)
options: `reload()` re-runs the loader with the same params and the status becomes `reloading`
Setting `value` locally moves the resource to the `local` state
Resources are the recommended way to send POST requests from a submit button
In v20 the `request` option was renamed to `params`
questions.explanation: Resources model reading data for the current params. Mutations belong in event handlers with `HttpClient`, followed by `reload()` or a local `update()`. The v20 API reshaping renamed `request` to `params` and gave `rxResource` a `stream` option.
optionNotes: A resource would re-send whenever tracked params change; mutations are not its job.

questions.question: Which function do you use to build a resource from an existing Observable-returning service method?
questions.explanation: `rxResource` (from `@angular/core/rxjs-interop`) takes a `stream` function returning an Observable and unsubscribes from the previous one when params change.

questions.question: What is the main benefit of `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })` over listing the service in `appConfig.providers`?
options: It creates a new instance per component
It makes the service available before bootstrap
It is tree-shakable: if nothing injects it, it is removed from the bundle
questions.explanation: Both give an app-wide singleton, but `providedIn: 'root'` lets the bundler drop unused services.

questions.question: A `CartService` is `providedIn: 'root'`. `CheckoutPage` also lists it in its `providers`. What happens?
options: `CheckoutPage` and its children get a separate instance; the rest of the app shares the root one
Angular throws a duplicate provider error
All components switch to the component instance
questions.explanation: A component provider creates an element-injector instance that shadows the root one for that subtree. This is a classic "state not shared" bug.

questions.question: How many instances of `LruCache` are created?
options: It throws because a class cannot be provided twice
questions.explanation: `useClass` creates a new instance for the `Cache` token, separate from the `LruCache` provider. `{ provide: Cache, useExisting: LruCache }` would alias both tokens to one instance.

questions.question: You need to inject a config object described by a TypeScript interface. What do you use as the DI token?
questions.explanation: Interfaces disappear at runtime, so they cannot be DI keys. `InjectionToken<T>` is a typed runtime token.

questions.question: What happens when this button is clicked?
options: It throws NG0203 because `inject()` is called outside an injection context
It creates a new instance each click
questions.explanation: `inject()` works only while Angular is creating something through DI (field initialisers, constructors, factories, functional guards and interceptors) or inside `runInInjectionContext`. Inject in a field instead.

questions.question: In what order does Angular search for a token requested by a component?
options: Root injector first, then the component, then its parent components
Only the root environment injector, because services are global
Own element injector, parent element injectors, then environment injectors (route, root, platform)
Environment injectors first, then element injectors from the root down
questions.explanation: Element injectors are searched first, walking up the component tree. If none provides the token, resolution continues in the environment injector hierarchy. The null injector throws unless `optional: true`.

questions.question: Which statements about multi providers are true? (Select all that apply)
options: `inject(TOKEN)` returns an array of every value registered with `multi: true` for that token
A later multi provider replaces earlier ones
questions.explanation: Each provider with `multi: true` contributes one entry to an array. They work with `useClass`, `useValue`, `useFactory` and `useExisting`. The legacy `HTTP_INTERCEPTORS` also relied on them.
optionNotes: Without `multi`, the last provider wins; with it, values accumulate.
Any provider kind can be multi.

questions.question: A nested menu component needs the menu instance from its parent, not itself, even though both are the same class. Which option do you pass to `inject(Menu, ...)`?
questions.explanation: `skipSelf` starts the lookup at the parent injector, skipping the current element. Combine with `optional: true` for the top-level menu that has no parent.

questions.question: In a signal-based service store, how should state be exposed to components?
options: As public `WritableSignal`s so components can update them
As read-only signals (for example via `asReadonly()`) with methods for updates
questions.explanation: Keep writable signals private so the store is the only owner that changes state. Components read signals and call intent-revealing methods.

questions.question: In NgRx Store, what is the only place where state changes?
questions.explanation: Reducers are pure functions that take the current state and an action and return new state. Effects handle side effects and dispatch actions; selectors read.

questions.question: Where should the current page number and filter of a list page usually live?
options: In the URL query parameters, bound to component inputs
questions.explanation: URL state makes the page shareable, bookmarkable and refresh-safe. With `withComponentInputBinding()` the query params arrive as inputs. Duplicating them in a store creates two sources of truth.

questions.question: What is the problem with this reducer?
options: Nothing, it is idiomatic NgRx and works fine
A reducer should return `void` and let the store merge changes
Reducers cannot call array methods such as `push`
It mutates state, so memoised selectors and OnPush views may miss the change
questions.explanation: Reducers must return new immutable state. Mutating keeps the same references, breaking memoisation, change detection and time-travel debugging. Return `{ ...state, orders: [...state.orders, order] }`.

questions.question: What is a facade in Angular state management?
options: A component that renders the whole state tree
A service that exposes a simple API to components and hides how state is implemented
A route guard that checks state
questions.explanation: Components call facade methods and read its signals without knowing whether NgRx, SignalStore or a plain service is underneath, so the state layer can change independently.

questions.question: Which are good reasons to choose NgRx Store over signal services? (Select all that apply)
options: Many teams and features react to the same events and you want a traceable action log
You need Redux DevTools time-travel debugging
The app has a single form and a few lists
questions.explanation: NgRx Store pays for its ceremony with explicit events, devtools and effects for orchestration. For small apps, signal services or SignalStore are simpler.
optionNotes: This is where NgRx boilerplate costs more than it gives.

questions.question: In NgRx SignalStore, how is state updated inside `withMethods`?
options: By dispatching actions to a reducer
By calling `store.set()` on the root signal
questions.explanation: SignalStore exposes state as read-only signals; `patchState` applies immutable partial updates. Observable-based side effects can use `rxMethod`.

questions.question: How do you lazy load a single standalone component for a route?
questions.explanation: `loadComponent` takes a function returning a dynamic import; the bundler emits a separate chunk loaded on first navigation. `loadChildren` is for a set of child routes.

questions.question: Users without the admin role must not even download the admin feature chunk. Which guard do you put on the lazy route?
questions.explanation: `canMatch` runs during route matching, before lazy code is loaded; if it returns false the router tries the next route. `canActivate` runs after matching, when the child routes have already been loaded. `canLoad` is the deprecated predecessor.

questions.question: Navigating from `/orders/1` to `/orders/2` keeps showing order 1. Why?
options: The component instance is reused, so `ngOnInit` does not run again and the snapshot is stale
The router caches HTTP responses for routes with the same path
Route params are read-only after the first navigation
questions.explanation: Default route reuse keeps the instance when only params change. Derive data reactively from the param: a signal input feeding `httpResource`, or `paramMap.pipe(switchMap(...))`.

questions.question: What does `withComponentInputBinding()` do?
options: Enables two-way binding on router links
Binds route params, query params, data and resolved values to matching inputs
questions.explanation: With it, `id = input<string>()` receives `:id` without injecting `ActivatedRoute`, and because inputs are signals, derived data updates when the param changes.

questions.question: What is the best thing for a functional `canActivate` guard to return when the user is not logged in?
questions.explanation: Returning a `UrlTree` or `RedirectCommand` makes the router cancel the current navigation and redirect as one operation, avoiding race conditions with a separate `navigate` call.

questions.question: Which statements about guards and security are true? (Select all that apply)
options: Guards run in the browser and can be bypassed
The API must still authorize every request
A `canActivate` guard on a `loadChildren` route stops its child-routes chunk from being downloaded
`canMatch` on a `loadChildren` route avoids downloading its chunk for users who fail it
questions.explanation: Guards are UX: they control navigation, not data access. `canMatch` runs during matching, before `loadChildren` is fetched; `canActivate` runs after matching, and the router has already loaded the child routes it needed to match.
optionNotes: The child routes are loaded during matching, before canActivate runs.

questions.question: In what order does the router run these during a navigation?
options: canDeactivate on the routes being left, then canActivateChild/canActivate, then resolvers
All guards and resolvers run in parallel for speed
questions.explanation: After matching (where `canMatch` runs), the router checks `canDeactivate` for routes being left, then activation guards from parent to child, and only if all pass, runs resolvers before activating components.

questions.question: What does `withPreloading(PreloadAllModules)` change?
options: Lazy route chunks are downloaded in the background after the app starts, so later navigations are faster
All routes are eagerly bundled into main.js
Resolvers run before the app bootstraps
Guards are skipped for preloaded routes
questions.explanation: Lazy routes stay separate chunks and the initial load is still small, but the router fetches them in the background after the initial navigation. Guards still run when the user actually navigates.

questions.question: Which forms approach defines the form model in the component class with `FormGroup` and `FormControl`?
questions.explanation: Reactive Forms build the control tree in code and connect it with `[formGroup]` and `formControlName`. Template-driven forms build it from `ngModel` directives in the template.

questions.question: Why is `form.value` typed as `Partial<...>` in typed Reactive Forms?
options: Because the form may not be submitted yet
Because async validators may be pending
Because disabled controls are excluded from `value`
questions.explanation: `value` omits disabled controls, so any key may be missing. `getRawValue()` includes disabled controls and is fully typed.

questions.question: What does `email.value` contain after `reset()`?
questions.explanation: A plain `FormControl` resets to `null`, which is why its type is `string | null`. With `nonNullable: true` (or `NonNullableFormBuilder`) it resets to its initial value.

questions.question: Where should a "password and confirm password must match" validator be attached?
options: In the template with a directive
On the parent `FormGroup` containing both controls
questions.explanation: Only the group sees both values. A group-level `ValidatorFn` returns an error such as `{ passwordsMismatch: true }` on the group.

questions.question: Which interface must a custom component implement so it works with `formControlName` like a native input?
questions.explanation: `ControlValueAccessor` (`writeValue`, `registerOnChange`, `registerOnTouched`, optional `setDisabledState`) bridges the form control and the component. Register it with `NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR`.

questions.question: Which statements about async validators in Reactive Forms are true? (Select all that apply)
options: They run only after all sync validators pass
While running, the control status is `PENDING`
They always run before sync validators
A new value cancels the pending validation from the previous value
questions.explanation: Angular skips async validators while sync validators fail, marks the control `PENDING` while they run, and switches to the latest value. Use `updateOn: 'blur'` or debounce to limit requests.
optionNotes: The order is sync first, then async.

questions.question: What is the most accurate description of Signal Forms in Angular v21?
options: A stable replacement that deprecates Reactive Forms
A wrapper that converts `valueChanges` to signals
An experimental API: data lives in a signal and `form()` derives fields with signal state
questions.explanation: Signal Forms (`@angular/forms/signals`) were introduced as experimental in v21, and became stable in v22. Reactive Forms remain supported and are not deprecated.

questions.question: This code freezes the browser. Why?
options: `setValue` inside its own `valueChanges` emits again, causing an infinite loop
`valueChanges` cannot be subscribed to in the constructor
`trim()` is not allowed on form values
questions.explanation: Each `setValue` emits `valueChanges`, which calls `setValue` again. Pass `{ emitEvent: false }`, or better, normalise the value on submit or in a ControlValueAccessor.
